name: Igbo nationalism
summary: Igbo nationalism is the ethnic nationalism of the Igbo people of southeastern Nigeria. It ranges from Biafran secessionism (Ojukwu's 1967 secession, MASSOB, IPOB) to demands for restructuring and fair representation within Nigeria, and also includes Igbo cultural revival and communal economic development. Its core claims are a right of self-determination, resentment of post-1966 marginalisation and the loss of eastern oil revenue, and pride in Igbo enterprise and culture.
scope: Mainstream Igbo ethno-nationalism as documented in the Ahiara Declaration (1969), the Igbo State Union and Ohanaeze tradition, MASSOB and IPOB. Biafran independence is treated as the dominant strand, with Ohanaeze-style restructuring as the moderate wing. Most economic, social and cultural questions are unaddressed by sources and answered by inference at low confidence.

sources.title: Igbo nationalism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Strands of the ideology (self-determination, cultural revival, economic development), history from the Igbo State Union to MASSOB, economic grievances.

sources.title: The Ahiara Declaration (1969)
sources.author: C. Odumegwu Ojukwu / Biafran National Guidance Committee
sources.usedFor: Biafra's founding principles: self-determination, popular sovereignty, communal trusteeship of property, equality, anti-corruption, religion, foreign policy.

sources.title: Indigenous People of Biafra
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Contemporary separatist aims, referendum demand, methods, grievances, armed wing, state response.

sources.title: Ohanaeze Ndigbo
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Mainstream Igbo socio-cultural body seeking Igbo political representation within Nigeria.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Ahiara stresses mutual responsibility and care for fellow citizens in need, so state-backed health care is an inference, not a documented demand.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Ahiara promises equal pay for equal output and rejects class privilege; a minimum-wage position is inferred from that.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Igbo society is described as entrepreneurial, yet Ahiara treats property as held in trust for the community, so adherents lean both ways.

public-ownership.rationale: Ahiara says all property belongs to the community and the state may intervene, but also backs private enterprise; no stated rail or utility policy.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Ahiara warns against large private fortunes held beyond community trust, from which higher taxes on the wealthy are inferred.

unions-good.rationale: Sources do not discuss unions; communal solidarity points mildly positive but the entrepreneurial tradition points the other way.

property-fundamental.rationale: Igbo commercial culture values property and enterprise, but Ahiara says property is held in trust for the community and the state may override it.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Ahiara rejects foreign economic exploitation and large private accumulation, from which tighter corporate regulation is inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: Ahiara's stress on helping citizens in need and communal duty makes welfare cuts unlikely to be favoured; inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: Communalism is stressed, but the documents say nothing on worker ownership and Igbo economic culture is mostly small-trader private business.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Adherents have faced state security forces and a terror designation of IPOB, but the sources give no position on surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: No source addresses drugs; the socially conservative, church-influenced setting suggests opposition, inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: IPOB's own rhetoric is ethnically charged and it faces speech prosecutions; adherents are split and sources are silent.

strong-leader.rationale: Ahiara says leaders are servants who can be removed and sovereignty belongs to the people, which cuts against strongman rule.

state-harmful.rationale: Ahiara envisions a strong, progressive Biafran state; the movement wants its own state, not none.

limit-guns.rationale: The movement's armed wing, the Eastern Security Network, sits uneasily with gun limits, but no source states a position.

empower-police-military.rationale: Igbo nationalists complain of heavy military presence and extrajudicial killings by Nigerian forces, so more federal police and army power is opposed.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; Ahiara's moral tone and a Christian-majority base suggest opposition, inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: Self-determination for the Igbo and demands to control regional resources imply devolution, though the aim is a state rather than local councils as such.

rehabilitation.rationale: Ahiara demands punishment of corrupt officials; nothing is said on prisons generally.

traditional-family.rationale: Communal social life and church-influenced norms suggest support, but the sources do not discuss family structure directly.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Igbo nationalist and church opinion is broadly socially conservative, inferred.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the predominantly Christian, socially conservative base.

more-religion-public.rationale: Ahiara frames Biafra as a Christian island against Islamic expansion yet rejects religious divisions inside Biafra.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Ahiara condemns racist indifference and the exploitation of Black people; supporting redress is inferred and is mostly framed in Igbo terms.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; Ahiara's equal pay for women is the only gender position documented.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Cultural preservation and revival of Igbo culture is one of the three strands the Wikipedia article gives for Igbo nationalism.

gradual-change.rationale: IPOB says it seeks no middle ground and wants to restore sovereignty, which is not gradualist.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration into Igboland is not an issue the sources raise; Igbo nationalists mostly object to Igbo emigrants' treatment elsewhere in Nigeria.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Adherents appeal to the UN and the international community for recognition, but sovereignty is the goal; no stated position.

free-trade.rationale: Igbo traders thrive in open markets, but Ahiara rejects foreign economic exploitation; split.

nation-first.rationale: Ahiara puts Biafran survival and self-determination first and rejects dependence on foreign powers.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Ahiara criticises Western indifference to Biafran civilian suffering, from which support for outside intervention is inferred.

open-borders.rationale: The movement seeks its own sovereign border; open borders are not a stated aim.

limit-growth.rationale: Igbo nationalism stresses economic development, so growth limits are unlikely to be favoured.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not discussed; the development emphasis is real but not a statement about technology.

revolution-justified.rationale: Ahiara calls its struggle a revolution and secession a right of survival; modern IPOB and MASSOB mainly use nonviolent means, so this is moderate.

experts-over-public.rationale: Ahiara says sovereignty belongs to the people, from which deference to experts is inferred to be rejected.

central-planning.rationale: The documented Igbo economic ethos is trading and entrepreneurship, not planning; inferred.

socialized-markets.rationale: Ahiara's communal trusteeship has socialist flavour, but it also protects private enterprise; split.

land-value-tax.rationale: No Igbo nationalist source discusses land taxation, and nothing in its aims points either way.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Ahiara disfavours large private fortunes but Igbo family wealth-building (aku luo uno) is valued; not addressed.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; communal duty to the needy is stressed but no such scheme.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Ahiara rejects foreign economic exploitation and neo-colonial dependence; protection is an inference.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Igbo nationalism seeks to develop Igboland and Ahiara has a state-guided development ethos; inferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Igbo society is described as built on small traders and communal self-help, so wide ownership fits, but no source states it.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Ahiara endorses equal pay and a working economy of enterprise; abolition of money is foreign to it.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; the grievance over the post-war £20 currency swap concerns a state action, not central banking in principle.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Ahiara does not propose state-recognised wage bodies, and the sources are silent on bargaining structures.

one-party-rule.rationale: Ahiara places sovereignty in the people and leaders as removable servants, though wartime Biafra was in practice a one-leader state.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Ahiara vests sovereignty in the people; hereditary monarchy is not part of the programme, though Igbo traditional rulers exist.

democracy-best.rationale: Ahiara declares popular sovereignty, and modern groups seek a referendum, though adherents distrust majority rule in Nigeria.

direct-votes.rationale: IPOB's central demand is a direct vote on independence, which implies approval of referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: Not part of the programme; Ahiara has communal ideas but no councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: The Ahiara Declaration calls self-determination the Biafrans' inalienable right, and MASSOB and IPOB seek independence from Nigeria.

natural-rulers.rationale: Ahiara rejects class privilege and says social mobility is open to all.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Biafran leadership fought a war and IPOB has an armed wing, but MASSOB and most adherents use nonviolent methods, so a mild rejection.

war-builds-character.rationale: Biafra's war is remembered as genocide and mass starvation, not as character-building.

separate-church-state.rationale: Ahiara rejects religious division within Biafra but defines Biafra against Islam and was Christian in character.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Ahiara does not found law on scripture; modern Nigerian Igbo objections are to sharia in the north, not a call for Christian law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Ahiara has a strong-state conception and calls for public accountability of officials.

military-superiority.rationale: Not addressed; adherents seek security from Nigerian forces but state no aim of superiority.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Igbo nationalism is an ethnic nationalism seeking a self-determining Igbo homeland; the Wikipedia article calls it a set of ethnic nationalist ideologies.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Igbo nationalism sees history through ethnic marginalisation and colonial divide-and-rule, not class conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Ahiara promises equal opportunity and pay for equal output, not equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: IPOB claims precolonial sovereignty over its homeland, so indigenous authority over traditional land is inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Ahiara condemns British colonial and wartime conduct; reparations are inferred rather than stated.

civilizational-union.rationale: Adherents define themselves against Arab-Muslim expansion and the Nigerian union; shared-civilization union is not their model.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Entrepreneurial ethos clashes with communal trusteeship; unaddressed directly.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Ahiara stresses community trust and mutual obligation but also inalienable rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Sources on Igbo nationalism concern politics and development and give no environmental philosophy.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; large families are valued in Igbo culture and grievances stress Igbo numbers, inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The movement stresses economic development of Igboland, so a view of industry as disaster is unlikely.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Ahiara insists sovereignty belongs to the people and leaders are accountable servants; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are wary of state surveillance but no position is documented.

restore-past-order.rationale: IPOB speaks of restoring precolonial independence and Biafra, but the movement also stresses development and progress.

results-over-ideology.rationale: No source discusses how policy should be judged; the movement is driven by a defined national goal.

direct-action.rationale: IPOB uses marches and sit-at-home protests, yet Ohanaeze and others work through elections and lobbying; split.

means-match-ends.rationale: No source addresses this; movements range from nonviolent MASSOB to the armed ESN.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Contrary to the development emphasis; inferred.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Foreign to an ethos built on trade and specialised urban careers; inferred.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Ahiara has communal care for those in need but also equal pay for equal output.

production-for-use.rationale: Not addressed; Igbo economic culture is trade-oriented.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Igbo entrepreneurship treats profit as legitimate; inferred.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Ahiara rejects class dictatorship and vests power in the people.

collective-farming.rationale: Not documented; Igbo land is farmed in family holdings and many left for trade because of poor soil.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Ahiara blames white economic imperialism for oppression of Black peoples but does not theorise capitalism as a cause of great-power wars.

taxation-theft.rationale: Ahiara treats property as held in trust for the community and accepts state intervention.

harm-principle.rationale: The sources give no view on limits of state power over private conduct.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Ahiara stresses community and trusteeship, and the movement's claims are group rights of a people.

conscription.rationale: Biafra mobilised its population in war; modern movements do not address conscription.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed, though the movement's aim is exit from Nigeria.

state-as-business.rationale: Ahiara treats leaders as servants of a community, not the state as a firm.

positive-liberty.rationale: Ahiara's equal-opportunity and social-mobility commitments suggest freedom needs material means; inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: No source claims media or universities hold political power; Radio Biafra shows media matter to the movement.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Ahiara condemns racist hierarchy against Black people and demands equality.

organic-representation.rationale: Community-based bodies such as Ohanaeze and town unions matter, but no source states this as a constitutional principle.

total-state.rationale: Ahiara places power in the people and allows private enterprise.

national-rebirth.rationale: Ahiara calls for a healthy, dynamic and progressive new Biafra against a decadent Nigeria.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The aim is self-determination in the existing Eastern region; there is no expansionist goal in the sources.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Ahiara places sovereignty in the people, not in loyalty oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Ahiara promises equal opportunity and mobility and condemns domination.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Epistemology is not discussed in Igbo nationalist sources.

universal-morality.rationale: Not addressed; Christian influence suggests mild agreement but nothing stated.

single-common-good.rationale: Ahiara emphasises the community good, but nothing is stated on pluralism.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Igbo nationalists often identify with Israel and the Jewish people, and Kanu has voiced such sympathy, but the sources here do not document it.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Igbo nationalists treat Igbo living elsewhere in Nigeria as members of the homeland; return right is inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: Preserving and reviving Igbo culture is a core strand, and Igbo language preservation is part of that.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Ahiara has communal ideas but no workplace voting; the economy is mostly small trade.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education is valued but no source states a funding model such as vouchers.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not discussed in the sources.

economic-freedom.rationale: The movement valorises Igbo enterprise and complains of economic strangulation; inferred.

rule-by-example.rationale: Ahiara says leaders must set an example, not take bribes and be removable, which approximates this.

national-self-determination.rationale: Ahiara states the inalienable right to self-determination and IPOB wants a sovereign Biafra.

force-without-un.rationale: Not addressed; adherents seek UN recognition rather than act as a state.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Christian-influenced culture makes a reason-only view unlikely; inferred.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Sources do not discuss welfare eligibility; immigrants are not a movement concern.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; the self-help ethos suggests some sympathy but the sources say nothing.

class-collaboration.rationale: Communalism and the wealth-builds-the-home philosophy suggest cooperation over class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Cultural preservation is a core strand of Igbo nationalism.

dominated-front.rationale: Ahiara frames Biafra within the black man's struggle against Western domination and neo-colonialism.

workers-nation.rationale: Class organisation is not a concern; the nation is defined ethnically.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Ahiara promises equal employment and pay for women, while the culture is traditional; split.

ban-interest.rationale: Igbo commercial and banking culture accepts interest; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Ahiara condemns racism and the movement itself suffered ethnic persecution.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Ahiara rejects class privilege but not a Marxist state theory.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: About 70 percent of Nigeria's oil lay in the eastern region, a central economic grievance; adherents want that wealth developed for Igboland.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Immigration into Igboland is not discussed by the sources.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not an Igbo nationalist claim; their fear concerns Fulani and northern domination, not elite-driven immigration.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not discussed, though power sharing is demanded.

national-mission.rationale: Ahiara claims Biafra will stand for Black self-determination, but not that it should spread its government.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Ahiara calls the Nigerian government corrupt and decadent and demands accountability and punishment of corrupt officials.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Contrary to Ahiara's equal-worth commitments; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: IPOB cites extrajudicial killings and the Biafran genocide and seeks accountability for them.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Ahiara envisions an active state promoting development and equality.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Ahiara promises equal opportunity and condemns racial hierarchy, though IPOB rhetoric includes anti-Fulani sentiment.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Socialist theory is outside Igbo nationalism; Ahiara borrows Arusha-style ideas only loosely.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Nigeria is seen as a colonial creation of 1914 amalgamation, but this statement concerns settler states and is only loosely related.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Ahiara rejects religion-based division, and Igbo nationalists oppose sharia in northern states; inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Ahiara rejects religious divisions inside Biafra, and the movement is not concerned with conversion bans.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Cattle are not sacred in Igbo culture and IPOB's quarrel is with open grazing by herders, not slaughter.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Not addressed; Christian-mission schooling is part of Igbo history.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Marxist state theory is not part of the programme.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Ahiara says sovereignty and power belong to the people and that Biafrans were forced into Nigeria without consent.

population-transfer.rationale: Igbo nationalists were themselves victims of expulsion in the 1966 pogrom.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Adherents justify armed secession and defence of Biafra, and IPOB formed a security force, so an absolute rule against initiating force is unlikely; inferred.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The entrepreneurial ethos suggests partial agreement, but nothing is stated.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The movement is itself banned as terrorist by Nigeria and resists such proscription.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Ahiara's fear of domination by Nigeria and of Arab-Muslim and Western domination matches this idea; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Ahiara calls for accountable leaders; checks on power are an inference.

vanguard-party.rationale: Not part of the programme; Ahiara places power in the people.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Ahiara stresses help for citizens in need and against class privilege.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure policy is not addressed by the movement's sources.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labour law is not addressed by the sources.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Igbo nationalists attribute poverty to marginalisation and strangulation, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Ethnic nationalists argue ethnic plurality in Nigeria produced conflict; the article says British divide-and-rule politicised ethnicity.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Adherents have been victims of emergency and military powers.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls are not discussed; traders are strongly represented among Igbo.

party-controls-media.rationale: Radio Biafra and the movement rely on independent media; inferred.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation is not discussed in the sources.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Ahiara condemns official corruption but sets no pay rule.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party organisation is not discussed beyond Ahiara's accountability of leaders.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The movement leaves Nigeria to exercise its own sovereignty and seeks no middle ground.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Constitutional command arrangements are not discussed in the sources.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed; Igbo Christianity spans episcopal and other churches.

clerical-rule.rationale: Ahiara vests sovereignty in the people.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not an issue in Igbo nationalism, which seeks its own state rather than debating great-power wars.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Censorship of art is not discussed in the sources.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Ahiara says leaders should not extend terms beyond the people's mandate.

recall-officials.rationale: Ahiara says leaders are servants who may be removed by the people.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Not addressed; Biafra sought foreign recognition and allies.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Contrary to a landlord-and-trader economic culture; inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Eastern Security Network is a local armed force, but the sources do not state a general principle.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The Igbo are described as urbanised traders and professionals; inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Igbo nationalists want Igbo of the Southeast, South-South and elsewhere under one Igbo-led polity, and see the 1967 states creation as division.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Igbo society is described as prizing schooling and professional achievement.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Ahiara rejects racist hierarchy among peoples; inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: The sources do not address capital punishment, and adherents are likely divided.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from socially conservative, church-influenced opinion.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The curriculum question is not addressed in the sources.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from socially conservative opinion.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The Igbo nation is conceived as a people of shared descent and ethnicity.

minority-language-support.rationale: Igbo language preservation is central, and Igbo are a minority within Nigeria.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The sources do not address exemptions; Ahiara rejects religious division generally.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Communal culture favours conformity with custom; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Ahiara rejects neo-colonial dependence; debt cancellation is inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Ahiara ties political independence to economic independence and rejection of neo-colonial exploitation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Adherents demand a referendum or a new settlement, and Ohanaeze-aligned voices seek restructuring.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Ahiara rejects dependence on foreign powers but condemns Western indifference.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons are irrelevant to a movement without a state, and no source addresses them.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Popular sovereignty is the Ahiara principle; inferred.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are not discussed beyond the post-war currency grievance.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: IPOB refuses middle ground on its homeland.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Ahiara says property is held in trust for the community.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Ahiara criticised Soviet backing of Nigeria but gives no analysis of Soviet economy.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation philosophy is absent from the sources.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance doctrine is not discussed; Biafra lacked formal allies.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: IPOB regards Biafra as annexed into Nigeria without consent; inferred from its claim.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Not addressed; churches are central to Igbo life, so adherents resist curbs.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Head-of-state role is not discussed in the sources.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Biafrans experienced Nigeria's war against secession as genocide.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Ohanaeze and moderate adherents seek restructuring with strong regional autonomy as an alternative to independence.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Ahiara vests sovereignty in the people.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Ahiara disapproves of large fortunes; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: No source discusses nature versus nurture.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Ahiara demands accountable leaders and punishment of those who abuse office.

space-expansion.rationale: Space is wholly absent from the sources.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Constitutional theory of this type is not part of the sources.

leader-cult.rationale: Followers revere Ojukwu and Kanu, but no source advances a leader cult as doctrine.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not addressed by the sources.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Marxist theory of socialism is outside the sources.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not addressed; land is scarce in Igboland but no programme is stated.

refugee-return.rationale: The 1966 pogrom and civil war drove Igbo from northern and western homes, and abandoned-property grievances are part of the movement.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Igbo nationalists claim Igbo-inhabited areas beyond the old Eastern region on ethnic grounds.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Ahiara rejects religious division and Islamic law.

women-must-cover.rationale: Opposed to Islamic expansion and sharia as the movement perceives it.

common-currency.rationale: Not addressed; Biafra issued its own currency.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Igbo nationalism focuses on the Igbo, while IPOB has allied with Ambazonian separatists in Cameroon; mixed.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: IPOB says it seeks no middle ground and a state of its own, though Ohanaeze takes a more autonomy-oriented line.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Ohanaeze fights for Igbo rights across Nigeria while MASSOB and IPOB seek a homeland; split.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Igbo nationalist accounts of history stress colonialism and ethnic politics, though economic motives are noted.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not addressed in the sources.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are not discussed in the sources.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: A minority nationalist movement seeks protection against the national majority.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Ahiara promises equal opportunity regardless of sex but nothing on quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Ahiara emphasises self-reliance but not autarky.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade agreement standards are not discussed in the sources.

moral-incentives.rationale: Ahiara stresses duty to community and public conduct, but also equal pay.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Biafra's war and the Eastern Security Network involved armed action, but adherents mostly stress nonviolence.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Ahiara rejects class privilege and open mobility; inferred.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Cultural preservation is core, including teaching Igbo history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Ahiara condemns colonial rule and racist treatment of Black people.

patriotic-education.rationale: Igbo cultural revival implies teaching pride in Igbo identity; inferred.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Affirmative action debates are not part of Igbo nationalism, though adherents want fair federal appointments.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money creation is not discussed in the sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Crisis theory is not part of the sources.

delink-world-market.rationale: The Igbo thrive on trade and want development, so a break is unlikely.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Dependency theory is not part of the sources.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The movement arose partly from discrimination against Igbo businesses.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: A persecuted minority benefits from entrenched protection; inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Igbo nationalists reject the 1914 amalgamation as an imposed colonial settlement.

elective-rulers.rationale: Ahiara places sovereignty in the people and leaders accountable to them.

minority-veto.rationale: The sources do not discuss unanimity rules, though a minority nationalism could favour vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Ahiara condemns Nigeria's government as corrupt and justifies resistance to it.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliamentary versus monarchical supremacy is not relevant to the sources.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is not discussed in the sources.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not discussed in the sources.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Ahiara says talent and wealth are held in trust for the community.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Cultural criticism of this type is absent from the sources.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Hegemony theory is absent from the sources.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Ahiara condemns white economic imperialism and exploitation; inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Offices for native-born citizens are not discussed; the issue is Igbo exclusion from federal posts.

party-own-road.rationale: Communist party independence is irrelevant to the sources.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Ahiara stresses self-reliance and rejection of neo-colonial dependence.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The sources are not about settler-descendant relations.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: American history is outside the sources.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not addressed, although Biafran flags and memorials matter to the movement.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Gender policy debates of this type are outside the sources.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Ahiara claims governance rooted in traditional communal modes rather than imported forms.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Adherents' experience is of military rule and its violence.

paid-care-work.rationale: Outside the sources, which mention only equal pay for equal output.

filial-duty.rationale: Communal Igbo culture emphasises family obligations; inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil service recruitment is not discussed in the sources.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a socially conservative base.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Ahiara says leaders are servants removable by the people.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not discussed in the sources.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Ahiara says all property belongs to the community, but nothing on use-based tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Budget procedure is not discussed in the sources.

single-official-language.rationale: Igbo language preservation implies a place for Igbo alongside others, not a single sole language.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Ahiara rejects foreign exploitation, but land purchase by foreigners is not discussed.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Legal doctrine of this type is outside the sources, though adherents see structural marginalisation.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Biafra sought arms abroad, but a doctrine of arming foreign insurgents is not discussed.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Rejects domination by powerful foreign states.

corporate-influence.rationale: Ahiara condemns foreign economic exploitation; inferred.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: IPOB itself relies on foreign diaspora support and would oppose such curbs.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Population policy is not discussed in the sources.

residents-only-property.rationale: Igbo nationalists resent others' control of Igboland resources; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: Ahiara promises equal employment opportunity but not a job guarantee.

democratic-peace.rationale: International relations theory is outside the sources.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Adherents deny duty to obey Nigeria's state but accept legitimate Biafran authority.

non-intervention.rationale: Ahiara criticises foreign support to Nigeria yet seeks foreign intervention for Biafra.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not discussed in the sources.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: IPOB's ideology includes anti-Fulani and anti-Muslim sentiment but it is not a doctrine of conspiracy.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from social conservatism.

local-production.rationale: Localism in production is not discussed in the sources.

informal-organisation.rationale: IPOB, MASSOB and Ohanaeze are organised bodies.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Adherents appeal to international law and self-determination against Nigerian law.

religious-nation.rationale: Ahiara rejects divisions by religion within Biafra, even though it is largely Christian.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Control of eastern oil revenue is a central grievance and the article notes that about 70 percent of Nigeria's oil lay in the old Eastern Region.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Ahiara supports private enterprise and personal ownership under trust.

defeat-communism.rationale: Ahiara criticised the Soviet Union's support for Nigeria, but communism is not its focus.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Igbo communities build schools and services through self-help alongside the state; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: Ahiara treats Biafra as a Christian society.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Marxist historical judgements are outside the sources.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Ahiara promises equal pay but links no further economic change to women's equality.

socialized-care.rationale: Public provision of domestic work is not discussed in the sources.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not discussed in the sources, which address revival only.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not discussed in the sources, though the Aburi Accord matters historically.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Ahiara communalism is rooted in traditional communal governance but not small property-sharing communes.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Ahiara sketches its own communal order between private enterprise and state ownership.

historical-land-claim.rationale: IPOB claims precolonial sovereignty and restoration of its homeland.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Igbo nationalists draw identity analogies with the Jewish experience of genocide; denial is rejected.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from broad Nigerian Igbo social conservatism.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Ahiara places power with the people; the movement itself is repressed.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Ahiara condemns British colonial exploitation and neo-colonial dependence of Black peoples.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Ahiara frames Biafra against Islamic expansionism.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Ahiara says sovereignty belongs to the people.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectional theory is outside the sources.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from social conservatism.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a Christian base.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The sources do not locate themselves on a left-right axis.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist theory of labour is outside the sources.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Ahiara and IPOB's ideology are anti-Muslim in framing, but mainstream adherents distinguish Islam from Fulani domination.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Ahiara vests sovereignty in the people.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Workplace law of this type is not discussed in the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Ahiara blends private enterprise with state intervention and community responsibility.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The movement forms its own security force and seeks protection.

rich-first.rationale: The Igbo ethos accepts that enterprising individuals and regions get rich first and share through communal obligations.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Ahiara criticised both Western and Soviet backing of Nigeria.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Ahiara says sovereignty is with the people.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not addressed, though Igbo rotating credit unions are traditional.

property-franchise.rationale: Ahiara promises equal opportunity and sovereignty with the people.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist theory is outside the sources.

reification.rationale: Marxist theory is outside the sources.

racial-franchise.rationale: Ahiara promises equal opportunity regardless of origin; Biafra was multi-ethnic, though Igbo dominant.

online-participation.rationale: Not stated in sources, though IPOB organises heavily online.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Igbo traders were victims of anti-Igbo violence.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Theological reform is not discussed in the sources.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Ahiara warns against accumulation of large fortunes.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Igbo nationalists demand rotation of the presidency, inclusion in federal offices and zoning.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Ahiara combines community care with the state.

term-limits.rationale: Ahiara says leaders should not extend terms beyond the people's mandate.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not discussed in the sources.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Ahiara promotes women's equality in employment but nothing on marriage.

rent-control.rationale: Housing policy is not discussed in the sources.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from enterprise culture.

uniformed-youth.rationale: IPOB has uniformed ESN, but a youth movement is not doctrine.

recognise-genocide.rationale: IPOB speaks of the Biafran genocide and seeks recognition of the 1967-1970 killings and starvation as genocide.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Ahiara promises equal pay for equal output and criticises unearned fortunes.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Biafra's war was framed as self-defence for survival.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: IPOB claims restoration of precolonial independence, implying continuity of the Igbo nation.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Feminist theory of this type is outside the sources.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Biafra Day and the movement commemorate those who died as martyrs for Biafra.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Ahiara's rhetoric of a Christian island in an Islamic sea has religious tone but not a doctrine.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Ohanaeze represents Igbo inside and outside Nigeria and diaspora ties matter.

culture-before-state.rationale: Wikipedia lists self-determination and cultural revival as separate strands, with adherents divided on order.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Igbo nationalism seeks Igbo control of Igboland's economy and complains of economic strangulation.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Igbo nationalists seek unification of Igbo-inhabited areas, and reject the 1967 splitting of the Eastern Region.

independent-unions.rationale: Union independence is not discussed in the sources.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Marxist theory is outside the sources.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Utilities ownership is not discussed beyond Ahiara's communal trusteeship.

second-chamber.rationale: Legislative design is not discussed, though a senate-style representation of regions is plausible.

municipal-property.rationale: Municipal ownership is not discussed in the sources.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Aburi Accord confederal arrangements were a Biafran demand before secession, and Igbo moderates still seek confederal restructuring.

family-wage.rationale: Ahiara has equal pay for equal output; nothing on family wage.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation is not discussed in the sources.

person-over-state.rationale: Ahiara balances individual trusteeship with community claims.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Ahiara's Christian framing implies a spiritual dimension.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Igbo regional autonomy is sought as secure, not revocable by Abuja.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Ahiara frames a shared Black struggle, but the movement's group is ethnic.

racial-pride.rationale: Ahiara affirms Black dignity and rejects racist denigration.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Biafra framed its war as defence.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Igbo nationalists regard language and culture as defining the Igbo nation across state and regional borders.

communal-electorates.rationale: Not discussed in the sources, though Ahiara rejects religious division.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Ahiara blames Britain and others for supporting Nigeria against Biafra and for colonial imposition.

free-public-college.rationale: Not addressed; education is highly valued but no policy stated.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Oil-region pollution in the Niger Delta is an Eastern grievance, but the sources set out no taxation policy; adherents are not committed either way.

future-generations.rationale: Ahiara treats the land and resources as held in trust for the people, from which a duty to hand them on is inferred.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The sources do not address women's distinct values; the Ahiara Declaration stresses equality of citizens, and adherents are not committed either way.

arms-reduction.rationale: Biafran separatism grew out of a war and IPOB has an armed wing, while Ahiara also stresses peace; adherents are split and the sources set no arms policy.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Ahiara stresses openness and accountability of rulers to the people, so open treaty-making is inferred rather than documented.

capital-controls.rationale: The sources show grievance over lost oil revenue but no position on capital flows; Igbo business culture favours enterprise and trade, so adherents are not committed.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Biafran leaders sought a state with its own army, so a state monopoly on arms is inferred; IPOB's armed wing makes it contested.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The Ahiara Declaration frames resistance as a duty to defend the people, so refusing orders in a defensive war is unlikely; inferred.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The sources give no labour policy; Igbo communal enterprise favours trading and self-employment, so adherents are split.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: The movement has no recorded position on tax credits.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no inference possible.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The Ahiara Declaration attacks neo-colonial economic exploitation, from which support for restructuring the world economy is inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: IPOB and Biafran secessionists seek to replace the Nigerian federal state, while Ohanaeze seeks restructuring; the stance on smashing it is inferred.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The Ahiara Declaration envisions a Biafran society with its own system of communal and egalitarian development rather than a fixed blueprint; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Oil revenue grievances concern ownership, not ecosystem accounting; the sources are silent.

sacred-nation.rationale: Igbo nationalism holds the Igbo people to be an enduring community with a shared destiny, though the sources do not describe it as sacred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: The movement has no recorded position on student debt.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Igbo nationalists argue that the Nigerian state marginalises the east and takes its oil revenue, which matches an internal colonial analogy.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The Ahiara Declaration appeals to human dignity and rights, from which a shared human nature is inferred.

public-service-media.rationale: The sources do not address public media funding.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Igbo nationalists include Christians and traditionalists; the sources give no shared position.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from Ahiara's emphasis on mutual responsibility and communal development; no scheme is documented.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Not addressed by the sources and anachronistic for an ethnic nationalism without a state.

workers-own-party.rationale: Igbo nationalist organisations are ethnic, cross-class bodies; a class-based party is inferred to be outside their programme.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not documented; inferred from Ahiara's modernising, welfare-oriented outlook.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Customary Igbo practice restricts women's inheritance and adherents are divided between custom and reform; not documented.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Igbo nationalism treats Igbo dialects as one language and one people; inferred from its cultural revival strand.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Oil-revenue grievances are central but no position on tort versus agency regulation is documented.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Ohanaeze brings traditional rulers into Igbo representation, so an advisory role is inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no clear position can be inferred.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed; an ethnic nationalism without its own state has no documented immigration policy.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Sources do not address union membership rules; no stated position, so adherents are split.

voter-id.rationale: No stated position; Igbo nationalists distrust Nigerian electoral processes but the sources do not address voter identification.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The Ahiara Declaration stresses popular sovereignty and a pluralistic Biafra, from which equal treatment of religious interpretations is inferred.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The Ahiara Declaration grounds legitimacy in popular sovereignty and the people's choice of rulers, inferred to favour electoral legitimacy.

premarital-sex.rationale: Mainstream Igbo nationalism is rooted in a largely Christian, socially conservative society; a conservative view is inferred, not stated in the sources.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Movements such as IPOB rely on online broadcasting and have been targets of Nigerian state censorship, so opposition is inferred.

negative-income-tax.rationale: The Ahiara Declaration favours communal and state-guided development; a market-style cash transfer replacing welfare is inferred to be unwelcome.

women-suffrage.rationale: Nothing in the sources denies women political rights and the Ahiara Declaration invokes the whole people's sovereignty; equal rights are inferred.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from the movement's strong Christian cultural identity; it did not frame religion as oppressive.

race-social-construct.rationale: Igbo nationalism is ethnic rather than racial and the sources take no view on racial categories; adherents are split.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: No stated position in the sources; adherents are split between support for modern governance and conservative views.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Sources do not address first-claim land ownership, and Igbo land tenure is largely communal and family-based, so adherents are split; inferred only.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Biafran nationalists present the 1966 pogroms and the war as atrocities and seek international accountability; supporting international trials is inferred from that.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Igbo nationalism is mostly Christian in its base but sources give no doctrinal position on scripture; inferred as split.

gendered-self-government.rationale: The Ahiara Declaration stresses equality and full participation of all citizens, from which guaranteed participation of women is inferred.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The Ahiara Declaration's socialist-leaning language sits beside strong Igbo private enterprise, so defending a planned state is not a documented position and adherents would split.

indirect-election.rationale: Ahiara calls for elected rulers answerable to the people, which favours direct popular election over delegate selection.

national-church-status.rationale: Ahiara does not give any church legal privilege; Nigerian Igbo nationalism is multi-denominational, so special status is inferred as unwelcome.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Ohanaeze-style restructuring demands regional autonomy for ethnic homelands within Nigeria, and Biafran nationalists go further to independence.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: IPOB's central demand is a referendum for Biafrans to decide their own status, which applies the same principle to the disputed question of Igbo territory.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Biafran secessionists reject Nigeria's colonial-era borders as imposed, so keeping them is inferred as disfavoured.

simple-living.rationale: Igbo nationalism prides itself on commercial enterprise and ambition, so a limited-needs ideal is not a documented value; inferred disagreement.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Indigenous-land authority was answered favourably in this audit from IPOB's homeland claims; restricting outsider settlement is a weak inference from that.

equal-conscription.rationale: Conscription was answered neutral in this audit and sources do not discuss gender and the draft; inferred as split.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Igbo nationalism stresses the Igbo homeland and the defence of the people's land; a duty to protect it follows from its self-determination claim.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Igbo nationalists, notably IPOB, have been victims of state killings and the Ahiara Declaration stresses justice; opposition is inferred.

close-ties-china.rationale: The sources do not address China; Biafra and its successors sought support from many outside states, so no direction is inferred.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Ohanaeze seeks representation for Igbo people throughout Nigeria, so support for kin outside the core region is inferred.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The Ahiara Declaration declares the land and resources held in communal trusteeship for the people.

self-ownership.rationale: The Ahiara Declaration stresses equality and dignity of the individual; full self-ownership is inferred from that.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The sources record no position on consumption taxes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The sources record no position on targeted versus universal social spending.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Ahiara rests on popular sovereignty and the movement works through bodies such as Ohanaeze; bypassing them for a leader is inferred to be disfavoured.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The Ahiara Declaration condemns corruption and favouritism and calls for equality of opportunity.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The Ahiara Declaration addresses religion as a matter for all citizens; separating politics from denomination is inferred.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The strands of Igbo nationalism combine cultural revival with enterprise and economic development, so pairing modernity with heritage is inferred.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The sources are silent on divorce and adherents hold varied views.

national-resource-control.rationale: Loss of eastern oil revenue is a core grievance and the demand for control of local resources runs through Biafran and IPOB claims.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred: the sources stress Igbo enterprise and communal trusteeship but never say whether justice depends on process or equality; adherents are split.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not addressed by Igbo nationalist sources; adherents have no settled view.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Racism in the racial sense is not the movement's frame; its grievance is ethnic marginalisation within Nigeria, so the question does not fit it cleanly.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred: IPOB and the Ahiara Declaration claim a right to resist an illegitimate state, but moderate Ohanaeze-style adherents work within Nigerian law, so the strands are split.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is about self-determination and adherents have no settled view on automation.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred from its demand for self-determination and an independent Biafra, which favours a world of many independent states.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred from the Ahiara Declaration's stress on enterprise and communal trusteeship, which does not rest on a labour theory of value.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred: Igbo nationalism is ethnic and pro-enterprise rather than worker-centred, so it neither joins nor opposes the pairing.

material-over-identity.rationale: Not addressed; Igbo nationalism is not a left project and the question is not its own.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred from its pro-enterprise, anti-authoritarian stance, which does not favour communist one-party rule.

missingStatements.text: A people who face persecution within a state may form their own independent state.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1966 pogrom and the civil war are the founding grievance, and Ahiara presents secession as the right of a people to survive.

missingStatements.text: Public offices and national posts should be shared among a country's ethnic regions by rotation or quota.
missingStatements.rationale: Exclusion from high federal office since Aguiyi-Ironsi is a core Igbo grievance, and Ohanaeze seeks Igbo political representation.

notes: Strands differ: IPOB seeks no middle ground and uses sit-at-home protests and an armed security network; MASSOB is nonviolent; Ohanaeze works for representation within Nigeria. Pro-Igbo and anti-Fulani or anti-Muslim rhetoric in IPOB is documented but is not shared by all adherents.
